checks.fix_hint: Regex the final HTML for `{{[A-Za-z0-9_]+}}` and `{{NN}}` tokens, standalone `TODO`/`FIXME`, `Lorem ipsum`, and generic placeholder names `\bModule [A-Z]\b` / `\bComponent [A-Z]\b`. Any match outside a <code>/<pre> block that is demonstrably documenting template syntax = fail.

Scan all `src=`/`href=` attribute values; fail if any resolves to a relative/local filesystem path (does not start with http://, https://, data:, blob:, #, mailto:, tel:). CDN links (https) and data:/blob: URIs are allowed; the artifact must be one portable file.

Per SKILL.md File Structure, assert the raw file starts with `<!DOCTYPE html>` (case-insensitive) and the parsed DOM contains `<meta charset>`, `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">`, and a non-empty `<title>`. Any missing piece = fail.

Parse <style>. Collect color custom properties in the top-level `:root{}`. Require a dark override block — `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark){:root{…}}` OR `:root[data-theme="dark"]{…}` — that redefines at least the core semantic set present in light (bg/surface/text/border/accent, case-insensitive substring). Fail if color custom props exist but no dark override block, or the dark block omits the core set.

If the document contains real links, assert the CSS has an `a`/`a:link`/`.prose a` rule setting `color` to a non-initial value (ideally `var(--accent)`). Fail if links exist but no link-color override rule is present, since UA-default link blue looks unstyled and has poor contrast on dark backgrounds.

Scan CSS selectors for a bare `.node` class token not nested under `.mermaid`, and scan HTML for an element whose class list contains the exact token `node`. Either = fail — Mermaid uses `.node` internally on SVG <g> elements, so page-level `.node` rules leak into diagrams; use `.ve-card` instead.

For CSS rules targeting block code containers (`pre`, `pre code`, `.code-block`, `.code-file__body`, `.dir-tree`), assert `white-space` is pre / pre-wrap / pre-line (never normal). Directory-tree / box-drawing containers (`.dir-tree`, or text containing ├└│─) must specifically be `pre` — pre-wrap soft-wraps and breaks connector alignment. Missing declaration or `normal` = fail.

checks.evidence: Page has a `<pre><code>` block over ~100 lines or that would render taller than ~500px.
checks.fix_hint: For `<pre><code>` blocks NOT inside `<details>`: (a) if newline-delimited line count > 100 → warn (avoid dumping full files; use outlines/collapsible/snippets); (b) if the block would render taller than ~500px, require `max-height` set and `overflow-y: auto|scroll`. Either unmet = warn.

Extend the 16px font-size / ≥1.5 line-height / ≤~75–85ch measure floors from `.prose p` to ALL running body prose (any multi-line

/list item that is not a caption/label/eyebrow/mono/code/table-cell), on page AND magazine profiles. Keep captions/labels/metadata/axis-labels exempt. Slides remain covered by min-slide-body-text-16px; poster/video-comp fixed canvases stay exempt (fixed-size type is intentional there).

Wait up to the configured Mermaid readiness timeout, then require every declared Mermaid container to contain an SVG and no Mermaid parse-error marker. A timeout is recorded as browser evidence and fails this check instead of aborting the verifier before findings are produced.

Load the page headlessly in both light and dark schemes; collect console messages of type 'error' plus failed network requests (non-2xx on linked resources). Fail on any error-level console message or non-2xx asset load, except a documented allowlist. Retry transient CDN 404s once before failing.

If the stylesheet defines any animation/transition with duration > 0, assert it also contains an `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce){…}` block that collapses animation/transition durations to near-zero for the animated elements or `*`. Missing = warn.

checks.evidence: Page profile only; skip when the artifact is fixed-canvas (root/body has fixed px width+height matching a slide/poster/magazine-deck canvas, a data-layout=slide|magazine|poster marker, or the document declares no @media(max-width) query at all).
checks.fix_hint: In the concatenated <style> text, locate the rule(s) targeting html and body (combined `html,body` or separate). Require ALL: `overflow-x:hidden` AND `overflow-x:clip` both declared, with the clip declaration appearing AFTER hidden in source order (progressive enhancement); `max-width:100%`; `margin:0`; `padding:0` covering html/body. Additionally assert NO rule targeting html|body|:root sets `overflow-x:scroll` (regex `(?:html|body|:root)[^{]*\{[^}]*overflow-x:\s*scroll` anywhere ⇒ violation). Browser corroboration (when a DOM is available): getComputedStyle(document.body).overflowX and getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).overflowX must each resolve to 'clip' or 'hidden', never 'scroll' or 'visible'. Fail if any required clause is missing or the scroll negative matches.

checks.evidence: Page profile, non-fixed-canvas (same profile guard as page-overflow-clip-contract).
checks.fix_hint: Regex the concatenated <style> for a universal border-box reset: a selector group covering `*` (optionally with `*::before,*::after`) whose declaration block contains `box-sizing:\s*border-box`. Also accept the inherit idiom (`html{box-sizing:border-box}` plus `*,*::before,*::after{box-sizing:inherit}`) or an equivalent reset-library rule. Fail only if no universal border-box coverage exists anywhere.

Regex for a `body` rule containing `overflow-wrap:\s*(anywhere|break-word)` or `word-break:\s*break-word`. Warn if absent. Advisory only — the authoritative failure for long-token overflow is the measured body-overflow gate; equivalent per-element `word-break` on long-token elements also satisfies intent.

checks.evidence: Page profile; only when a grid-template-columns declaration pairs a bare 1fr with a fixed-px track.
checks.fix_hint: Scan <style> grid-template-columns declarations for a bare `1fr` track directly adjacent to a fixed-px track and NOT wrapped in minmax(): match `grid-template-columns:\s*[^;]*\b\d+px\s+1fr\b` or `\b1fr\s+\d+px\b` within a declaration where that `1fr` is not the tail of a `minmax(` call. Any match is a violation (documented #1 root cause of horizontal overflow).

checks.evidence: Page profile with at least one `@media (max-width: Npx)` query.
checks.fix_hint: Extract every `@media` `max-width:\s*(\d+)px` value. Allowed standard set {768, 820}; sanctioned exceptions {640 (Nothing grid-lines), 1000 (responsive-nav.md TOC sidebar→bar collapse)}. Warn on any other max-width value.

checks.evidence: Page contains an element with class `pipeline`.
checks.fix_hint: Inside a mobile `@media (max-width:...)` block, the `.pipeline` rule must declare `flex-wrap:\s*nowrap`. Warn if .pipeline exists on the page but the mobile rule is missing or sets flex-wrap:wrap.

checks.evidence: Page contains an element with class `kpi-row`.
checks.fix_hint: Inside the mobile media query, `.kpi-row` should set `grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(<N>px, 1fr))` (N tolerant). Warn if .kpi-row is present but reduces to a fixed column count at mobile instead of an auto-fit minmax floor.

Load the page and, at BOTH viewports 390x844 and 1440x900, in BOTH prefers-color-scheme light and dark, assert `document.documentElement.scrollWidth - window.innerWidth <= 1` AND `document.body.scrollWidth - window.innerWidth <= 1`. Fail if the 1px tolerance is exceeded at any viewport/scheme combination. (1px tolerance replaces the doc's strict === to absorb browser sub-pixel rounding.)

At 390x844 (and 1440x900) in both schemes, evaluate `[...document.querySelectorAll('body *')].filter(el => el.clientWidth>0 && el.scrollWidth > el.clientWidth + 1 && getComputedStyle(el).overflowX === 'visible')`. The list must be empty; report {tag, className, scrollWidth, clientWidth} for each offender so the fix (add .scroll-x / min-width:0 / max-width:100%) can be targeted. Non-empty ⇒ fail.

At 390x844, for each direct child of such a container, if child.scrollWidth > child.clientWidth + 1 (child is overflowing its own box) AND getComputedStyle(child).minWidth resolves to a non-zero value (i.e. min-width:auto), flag as a shrink-refusing child. Gate strictly on measured child overflow to avoid failing grids whose children are naturally narrow.

At 390x844 (representing <=768px), for each such element assert getComputedStyle(el).gridTemplateColumns resolves to a SINGLE track (value is a single length/none, no internal space between track sizes). Covers both fixed-column named grids and the 2-column magazine hero. Skip .kpi-row (auto-fit exception).

checks.evidence: Page contains a <table>, .pipeline, .dir-tree, an inline diagram <svg>, or a .code-block.
checks.fix_hint: At 390x844, for each candidate wide element (table, .pipeline, .dir-tree pre, inline diagram svg, .code-block) that actually overflows (el.scrollWidth > el.clientWidth + 1), verify the element itself OR an ancestor within 3 levels has computed overflow-x in {auto, scroll} (i.e. a scroll container such as .scroll-x/.table-wrap/.mermaid-wrap or inline overflow-x:auto). If it overflows and no scroll container is found ⇒ violation. This subsumes the ~640px SVG threshold using measured overflow rather than the raw viewBox number.

checks.evidence: Page has a .dir-tree element, or a <pre> whose text contains box-drawing characters (├ └ │).
checks.fix_hint: For each such <pre>, assert getComputedStyle(el).whiteSpace is 'pre' or 'nowrap' (NOT 'pre-wrap' or 'normal') AND the element or an ancestor within 3 levels has overflow-x auto/scroll. Violation if wrapping is permitted (pre-wrap/normal) OR no horizontal scroll container exists.

At 390x844 (both schemes) collect elements where getComputedStyle overflowX or overflowY is 'clip'/'hidden' AND (scrollWidth>clientWidth+1 OR scrollHeight>clientHeight+1) AND the element has non-empty direct text content, EXCLUDING elements whose computed `-webkit-line-clamp` is not 'none' or `text-overflow` is 'ellipsis'. Emit the candidate list for the single profile-aware artifact review. Non-empty ⇒ warn (visual confirmation decides the ship-blocker).

At 390x844 (both schemes), for each position:fixed element with a non-transparent computed background, compute its bounding rect and find interactive/text elements (a, button, h1-h4, p, td, .sec-head) whose rects geometrically intersect it and paint beneath it. Emit overlap candidates for the single profile-aware artifact review. Non-empty ⇒ warn.

Assert no

element and no hero text-bearing element carries class `scroll-x`; assert card-grid containers are not themselves wrapped in `.scroll-x` (they should reflow to one column). A `.scroll-x` wrapper around a wide diagram that happens to live inside the hero is allowed — scope to text-bearing prose nodes, not any .hero descendant.

checks.evidence: Page has both a `.wrap` element and a `nav.toc`.
checks.fix_hint: Assert .wrap.firstElementChild is nav.toc (tag nav, classList includes 'toc'); assert all section content lives inside a `.main` child of .wrap (every .sec-head is a descendant of .main, none are direct children of .wrap); and assert the stylesheet contains a `.main{...min-width:0...}` declaration. Fail if the toc is not first, content leaks outside .main, or .main lacks min-width:0.

Assert every `.sec-head` element has a non-empty id; every `.toc a[href^="#"]` (excluding a '#'/'#top' back-to-top link) resolves via document.getElementById to an existing element; and the count of section .toc links equals the count of .sec-head elements.
Count .sec-head elements (or section .toc links). Warn if fewer than 4 — a near-empty TOC adds clutter.

checks.evidence: Source contains a `prepareWithSegments(` call (pretext label-measurement library in use).
checks.fix_hint: For each `prepareWithSegments(` call, require an awaited `document.fonts.ready` or `document.fonts.load(` earlier in the same script scope (before the call). Warn on any prepareWithSegments with no preceding fonts-ready await — measuring against fallback fonts yields wrong widths that drift every downstream box calc.

checks.evidence: Document contains an inline <svg> authored by the skill (heuristic: an <svg> whose element attributes reference var(--...) tokens, or that declares data-diagram-role).
checks.fix_hint: Regex diagram-body elements for hex color literals (#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}) and rgb()/rgba() literals appearing inside fill=, stroke=, or style= attributes. Exclude the :root/@media token-definition blocks and url(#...) references. Flag any literal color on a body element.

checks.evidence: Document contains an inline skill-authored <svg> diagram.
checks.fix_hint: Regex-scan diagram markup and flag any of: (a) box-shadow or SVG feDropShadow on nodes; (b) background-clip:text / -webkit-background-clip:text co-occurring with a linear-gradient on a title/heading; (c) pictographic emoji codepoints inside <text> content; (d) box-shadow or filter:blur combined with animation/transition/@keyframes (animated shadow); (e) writing-mode:vertical on arrow-associated <text>; (f) Tailwind class rounded-2xl or an rx/ry/border-radius of exactly 16.

checks.evidence: Inline skill-authored <svg> diagram present AND the active aesthetic is NOT an IDE-inspired one whose canonical palette specifies JetBrains Mono.
checks.fix_hint: Regex for "JetBrains Mono" in any font-family declaration (inline style, @font-face, or Google Fonts href) within diagram markup. Flag presence.
Parse numeric values of x, y, cx, cy, width, height, font-size, and gap/spacing across diagram SVG; assert each value % 4 === 0. Report every offending element+attribute+value.

checks.evidence: Inline diagram with node-name/title/description text identifiable (data-diagram-role tagging present) AND aesthetic is NOT Monochrome-Terminal. Warn-level heuristic fallback when tagging absent.
checks.fix_hint: For every <text> classified as a node name/title/description, resolve font-family and assert it is var(--font-body), not var(--font-mono). Additionally flag if var(--font-mono) is the majority face across body-classified text. Technical labels (ports/types/URLs/arrow labels/eyebrow kickers) may be mono.

checks.evidence: A diagram <svg>/<style> lives inside a document that already declares a :root token block (--paper/--ink) earlier in the cascade.
checks.fix_hint: Flag duplicate :root declarations of the diagram color-token names (--paper/--ink/etc.) within a single document — an embedded diagram must inherit host tokens rather than redeclaring them.

checks.evidence: Arrows and nodes are distinguishable via data-diagram-role or separate <g> groups.
checks.fix_hint: Assert the arrows group's document index precedes the nodes group; or, per connected component, assert every arrow-classified element's document index precedes the node elements it connects.

checks.evidence: A legend group is present in the diagram.
checks.fix_hint: Assert the legend group bbox sits within the bottom ~60px band of the viewBox; items lay out left-to-right (width >> height, x-coords monotonic and non-overlapping); a sibling line/rect with stroke=var(--rule) sits directly above it; and viewBox height >= bodyMaxY + ~50-70px headroom. Never float inside the diagram body.

checks.evidence: Arrow-label text is present (role tagging or arrow-associated <text>).
checks.fix_hint: For every <text> classified as an arrow label, assert the immediately-preceding sibling is a <rect> with fill resolving to var(--paper)/var(--paper-2). (Pixel-coverage of the rect over the text bbox is verified in diagram-text-clipping-overlap.)

checks.evidence: Elements carry data-diagram-role tagging (decision c). Warn-level heuristic count fallback when tagging absent.
checks.fix_hint: Count generic node elements (role=node), assert <=9; count arrow/transition elements (marker-end=url(#arrow*) or role=arrow), assert <=12. Exclude legend/annotation/axis elements from the node count.

checks.evidence: Inline diagram where the accent token/literal is resolvable.
checks.fix_hint: Count distinct elements whose fill or stroke resolves to var(--accent) (or the aesthetic's literal accent hex); assert count <= 2.

checks.evidence: Diagram type is detectable (data-diagram-type or structural signature) AND role tagging present. Warn-level fallback when tagging absent.
checks.fix_hint: Per detected type, assert count <= budget: sequence lifelines <=5; swimlane lanes <=5; ER entities <=8; nested containment levels <=6; tree depth <=4 and children-per-node <=5; layer-stack layers 4-6; venn set-circles <=3; pyramid/funnel layers 4-6; annotation callouts <=2; quadrant items <=12.

checks.evidence: Detected diagram type is flowchart, state-machine, or sequence.
checks.fix_hint: Flowchart: start/end rx=20, step rx=6, decision=diamond with <=3 outgoing arrows (else must nest), merge=filled <circle r=4>; every decision outgoing arrow has a text label; shape (not color) must be the semantic channel. State-machine: state rects rx=8, start=filled <circle r=6>, end=two concentric circles, transition label matches /^\S+(\s\[[^\]]+\])?\s*/\s*\S+/, transitions <= 2x state count, no 'from any state' fan-out. Sequence: lifelines vertical (x1~x2) with stroke-dasharray set, message arrows horizontal (y1~y2) with non-decreasing y in document order, activation bars width=8 stroke-width=0.8 fill~var(--muted) each with matched open+close, return arrows dashed, no lane dividers.

Assert axis lines cross at the plot-area geometric center; axis labels lie near the extreme x/y of each axis (not within a midpoint tolerance band); item dots have r=4; no item (x,y) sits within epsilon of x=centerX or y=centerY; any quadrant background rects all share the same fill.

Callout text font-style=italic and font-family=var(--font-display); leader path has stroke-dasharray set (never solid); a landing-dot <circle> exists at the leader terminus; count <=2 per diagram; neutral callout leader stroke-opacity~0.4 and text fill=var(--ink), focal callout leader+text fill=var(--accent). Non-overlap with content is verified in diagram-text-clipping-overlap.

Assert filter params baseFrequency in [0.01,0.04], numOctaves in [1,3], scale in [1,6], and a fixed seed attribute present. Find every element referencing that filter (directly or via a filtered ancestor); assert no <text> is among them or their descendants.

checks.evidence: A ranked/proportional diagram (pyramid, funnel, venn, timeline, bar) whose items carry data-value / data-percentage / data-cardinality attributes.
checks.fix_hint: Recompute expected geometry from the data and assert rendered geometry matches within a few px: pyramid/funnel layer width = maxWidth x (value/base); venn circle radius proportional to sqrt(cardinality); timeline event x-position proportional to real time delta across adjacent events (or a visible axis-break marker over anomalous gaps). Accent must not sit on the base/largest layer; widths monotonic in a single direction.

Render at 1440x900 (both schemes). Resolve the start and terminal points for line, path, polyline, and polygon connectors into viewport coordinates with getScreenCTM(). Pair data-diagram-source and data-diagram-target with nodes by data-diagram-id; when no target is declared, use the nearest tagged node. Assert a 6-10px air gap and no point-in-rect intersection at every declared endpoint. When data-diagram-source-anchor or data-diagram-target-anchor is left-center, right-center, top-center, or bottom-center, also assert that endpoint lands on the named side and aligns to its midpoint within 3px.

Render (1440x900, both schemes). For every <text> assert getBBox() is fully contained within the SVG viewBox and its intended container group's bbox. Pairwise collision-test all text bboxes and leader-line paths and assert no unexpected intersections (excluding intentional label-on-mask overlaps). For each arrow-label mask rect assert it contains its text bbox with >= ~4px margin per side.

checks.evidence: Mono-Industrial detected: Space Grotesk loaded as --font-body AND no Doto/Libre Baskerville/Manrope loaded (distinguishes from Nothing).
checks.fix_hint: Parse font-family declarations actually applied to elements (first non-generic name per stack only). (1) Distinct applied families ≤3 (Space Grotesk, Space Mono, +optional one Geist Pixel accent); fail if >3 or if >1 pixel-accent face loaded. (2) Geist Pixel @font-face present only if some element's resolved computed font-family (following --font-display var chain) uses it; warn if loaded-but-unused. (3) Distinct applied font-size values (var(--size-*), literal px, one clamp()=one size) ≤4 — display/section/body/caption per tokens.md; error if >4, warn at exactly 4 if the 4th isn't --size-section. (4) No font-weight resolving to 700/bold on any element whose family resolves to Space Grotesk/--font-display sans (check computed style so UA-default <b>/<strong> bold counts); distinct weights in use (excluding Space Mono 700) ≤2.

checks.evidence: Mono-Industrial detected (Space Grotesk body, no Doto/Libre Baskerville).
checks.fix_hint: Scan all color/background/border-color/fill/stroke literals. Whitelist documented grayscale values (#000, #f6f4f0, rgba(242,237,229,*), rgba(22,19,15,*) and var(--fg)/--text-*/--rule* forms) plus the six status hexes and var(--ok|--warn|--err). Fail on: any other hue-bearing literal; linear-gradient(/radial-gradient( in chrome; background-clip:text with non-monochrome color or -webkit-text-fill-color set to a hue; var(--ok|--warn|--err) used as background-color/fill on row/section selectors (tr,.row,.section,li) or as color on label-classed text (status marks the value/datum, never a container or label).

checks.evidence: Mono-Industrial detected AND profile is scrollable page.
checks.fix_hint: Find one fixed-position container (position:fixed with top/right offsets) holding exactly 3 co-located options whose text/aria-label match /light/i, /dark/i, /auto|system/i. Within it: each option's icon slot is an inline <svg viewBox='0 0 16 16'> with a <circle r='5'> (or proportionally equivalent viewBox scaling), rendered ~12x12; fail if the literal glyphs ○/●/◐ (U+25CB/25CF/25D0) are used as icons.

checks.evidence: Mono-Industrial detected AND profile is scrollable page.
checks.fix_hint: Sniff the base mode from bare :root token values (dark-first vs light-first). Assert the OPPOSITE-mode @media (prefers-color-scheme:…) block's selector is :root:not([data-theme='<base-mode>']) — not bare :root. Assert standalone :root[data-theme='light'] AND :root[data-theme='dark'] rule blocks both exist and define the full token set. Assert inline script persists to localStorage key 'mono-industrial-theme' via setItem/getItem, and removeItem (falling back to prefers-color-scheme) when the selection is system/auto.

checks.evidence: Mono-Industrial detected AND a theme toggle is present.
checks.fix_hint: Assert the active-state rule background matches color-mix(in srgb, var(--fg) 10%, transparent) (whitespace-tolerant) and active label color references var(--text-display) — never a new hue. Assert an @media (hover:hover)/pointer:fine rule collapses the pill to the active indicator paired with a :hover/:focus-within (or JS mouseenter/focus class-toggle) expansion, with no collapse under pointer:coarse. Assert a responsive rule moves the dock bottom-right with ≥44px touch targets at tablet/phone.

checks.evidence: Mono-Industrial detected AND page contains Mermaid diagrams (.mermaid or mermaid.initialize).
checks.fix_hint: In the toggle change handler, assert code that resolves palette via a mode function (checks data-theme then OS preference), clears/resets data-processed on .mermaid, restores stashed original diagram source text, and calls mermaid.run(. Additionally assert a matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)') addEventListener('change',…) triggers the same re-theme when data-theme is unset (live OS tracking).

Extract :root base and data-theme override custom-property declarations. After detecting base mode, string-compare --bg,--fg,--text-display,--text-primary,--text-secondary,--text-disabled,--rule,--rule-strong,--ok,--warn,--err against the exact hex/rgba values in tokens.md for BOTH light and dark modes. Fail on any deviation.

Scan CSS/JS. Fail on: any @keyframes glow/pulse/animated-shadow; any animation applied unconditionally (not scoped to :hover/:focus/.active/[data-*]); any IntersectionObserver toggling opacity/transform on scroll (scroll-reveal); any inline opacity:0 transitioned to 1 on load/DOMContentLoaded; any transition/animation-duration >120ms; any cubic-bezier spring/bounce on non-interaction elements. Require an @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block forcing ~0.01ms durations on *,*::before,*::after. For slide-deck structure, assert slide-changing property (transform/opacity) has no transition (instant cut; scroll-snap handles the step).

checks.evidence: Mono-Industrial detected AND page contains Mermaid.
checks.fix_hint: Parse mermaid.initialize themeVariables: primaryColor/secondaryColor/tertiaryColor/lineColor must resolve to grayscale nodeFill/nodeBorder/edgeColor values (not arbitrary hue). Any classDef setting fill/stroke may only use the six approved status hexes. Assert edge labels resolve to Space Mono uppercase 11px and node labels to Space Grotesk 15px (20px allowed in slide role).

checks.evidence: Mono-Industrial detected AND a real <table> is present.
checks.fix_hint: For <table> elements: no nth-child(even/odd) background-color (zebra); no border-left/right on td/th; row elements carry border-top:1px solid var(--rule); header cells resolve to --font-mono, uppercase, ~11px, var(--text-secondary); cells whose content is numeric (regex \d with %/currency/ratio) are text-align:right with font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums; assert no text-overflow:ellipsis, white-space:nowrap+overflow:hidden, or -webkit-line-clamp on cells (long text wraps, never truncates).

For label/caption/index/metadata-classed elements: font-family resolves to Space Mono, text is uppercase (text-transform or already-caps source), letter-spacing 0.08em–0.14em, not sentence-case prose with trailing colons. Date-like strings in metadata rows match /^\d{4}\s*·\s*\d{2}\s*·\s*\d{2}$/ (no slashes). Empty/error/loading state containers use inline Space Mono ALL CAPS bracketed text matching /^\[[A-Z0-9 .:\-]+\]$/ with no illustrations, multi-sentence

, or fixed-position toast.

Flag margin/padding/gap px literals not in {4,8,16,32,64,96} and not var(--space-*), excluding 1px hairlines and the toggle's 24px/44px. Flag any card-signature wrapper (border + background-color/fill + border-radius/box-shadow) that contains the page's primary display/hero element (never box the display element), and flag non-table/non-nav border dividers between sibling blocks as spacing-should-have-sufficed candidates.

checks.evidence: Mono-Industrial detected AND a .code-block / pre>code[class*='language-'] is present.
checks.fix_hint: Assert .code-block background resolves to #0a0a0a in both data-theme states (does not swap with --bg). Assert markup pre.code-block > code[class*='language-']. Assert no stock Prism theme (tomorrow/okaidia/twilight/etc.) is linked — only the custom Mono-Industrial token CSS. Assert no line-numbers/copy-button elements unless requested. Diff-line backgrounds use ~0.1-alpha green/red (never solid alpha=1). Flag code blocks >20 lines not wrapped in <details>.

Assert elements with role='hero'/top-level .ve-hero count ≤1. Count pattern-break candidate signatures (Geist-Pixel-styled elements; border-radius:50% among otherwise rectangular content; spacing gaps ≥2× the largest tier used elsewhere; font-size outliers beyond the declared scale). Flag if candidate count is 0 (sterile) or >1 (noisy) — this is the deterministic pre-filter feeding mono-one-surprise.

checks.evidence: A named aesthetic is detected (Mono-Industrial or Nothing).
checks.fix_hint: Render at 1440×900 in prefers-color-scheme light AND dark (and each data-theme override). In each mode: compute contrast ratio of --text-primary against --bg and assert ≥4.5:1; assert no text-bearing element resolves to a color within ~ΔE small of its own background (invisible-text guard); assert elements spec'd to stay fixed across modes (dark terminal code blocks, CTA-on-blue) do not flip. Fail if any mode has failing contrast or invisible text.

In the final HTML, count occurrences of each distinct @font-face{font-family:'X'} block and each library CDN <script src> (mermaid/chart.js/anime) and its init call; fail if any is duplicated. Count :root design-token declaration blocks defining core tokens (--bg,--fg,--text-*,--rule*,--space-*,--size-*,--ok/--warn/--err); fail if the same core token is (re)declared in more than the sanctioned base + data-theme override blocks (fragment/section CSS must not redefine root tokens).

checks.evidence: Nothing detected: Doto loaded AND Space Grotesk body AND no Libre Baskerville (distinguishes from Mono).
checks.fix_hint: Scan <link>/@import/font-family. Allowlist named families = {Doto, Space Grotesk, Space Mono}; flag any other named family, with an explicit hard-fail if 'Geist Pixel' appears anywhere (Mono's default must not leak into Nothing).

At a single canonical viewport, collect computed font-size across visible text elements, cluster within 1px tolerance; assert distinct-size count ≤3 (one Doto hero, one Space Grotesk body, one Space Mono caption). Nothing states the budget unconditionally — no numeric-hero exception. Error if >3.

Query elements whose computed font-family includes 'Doto'; assert exactly 1 uses it and its text is short (word count ≤6, not a paragraph/body block). Assert its computed font-size ≥48px (Decision (c): §4.1's 48px is authoritative; treat 36–47px as a warn band due to the §2-vs-§4.1 doc conflict; error below 36px).

Query candidate label elements (nav a, th, button text, .label/.unit/.kicker/section-kicker classes); assert each has computed font-family including 'Space Mono' AND (text-transform:uppercase OR raw text already all-uppercase).

Count elements where #D71921 / var(--accent) is actually APPLIED (painted) as a foreground, background, or border color across the DOM; assert ≤1. Diff the --accent token's literal value between the dark :root block and the light-mode override; assert identical (red is unchanged between modes).

Assert label-like elements (.label, th, nav items) do not have computed color equal to var(--success)/--warning/--accent. Assert row containers (tr, .stat-row) do not have those tokens as background-color. Confirm .value/.num elements ARE permitted to carry them.

Scan CSS. Fail on: any box-shadow value other than none; linear-gradient(/radial-gradient( outside a hero-vignette-scoped selector; backdrop-filter or filter:blur outside a .nav-dots/magazine-deck-scoped selector; border-radius >16px on .card/card-like selectors (buttons excluded). Also fail on any transition/animation declaration whose properties include transform, scale(, translate(, or box-shadow (hover feedback is border/text-color only). Where an explicit timing is set, durations should be 150–250ms (micro) or 300–400ms (view) with cubic-bezier(0.25,0.1,0.25,1).

Flag class/id names containing 'skeleton','toast','spinner'. Flag nth-child alternating background-color on table rows (zebra). Flag emoji Unicode ranges or multi-fill/filled inside buttons/nav. For elements explicitly marked as empty/loading/error states, flag >1 paragraph and require a bracket-notation pattern /^\[.*\]$/ somewhere in the state's text (e.g. [LOADING…], [NO DATA]).

checks.evidence: Nothing detected AND button-like elements exist.
checks.fix_hint: For primary/secondary buttons: computed font-family Space Mono, font-size ≈13px, text-transform uppercase, letter-spacing ≈0.06em, padding ≈12px 24px, min-height ≥44px. Count primary buttons (white bg + black text); assert ≤1 per screen. Collect secondary button border-radius values; assert all pill (~999px) OR all technical (4–8px), never mixed.

Detect each motif: (1) a Doto-family element; (2) ALL-CAPS Space Mono labels; (3) segmented progress bars (.progress/.seg); (4) dot-grid radial-gradient background; (5) bracket-notation text /\[[^\]]+\]/ inside a dedicated UI-state container; (6) a grid-break candidate. Count detected motifs; assert ≥3.

checks.evidence: Nothing detected AND a multi-series chart/legend exists.
checks.fix_hint: For multi-series charts, check whether series are distinguished ONLY by distinct fill/stroke colors with no accompanying opacity variation, hatch/pattern fill, or distinguishing legend text/shape. Flag color-alone differentiation.

At 1440x900 and 390x844: for vertical decks, each `section.slide` computed height == viewport height within +-2px and computed overflow-y == 'hidden'; for magazine, each `.page` computed width == window.innerWidth AND height == window.innerHeight within +-2px, and both `body` and `.mag` have computed overflow-y == 'hidden'. For every slide/page element assert element.scrollHeight <= element.clientHeight + 2 (no internal overflow), EXCLUDING known nested scroll containers (.mermaid-wrap, .table-scroll, .code-scroll and any descendant whose own computed overflow is auto/scroll). Also assert document.documentElement.scrollHeight <= clientHeight for magazine (no vertical scrollbar). Do NOT run at additional widths — these are fixed-canvas profiles, not responsive.

Vertical: computed `scroll-snap-type` of the vertical deck container resolves to `y mandatory`. Magazine: computed `scroll-snap-type` of `.mag` resolves to `x mandatory` (or longhand x/mandatory) AND no element in the document declares `scroll-snap-type: y ...` (magazine must not mix in the vertical engine). Use getComputedStyle after load so shorthand/longhand both resolve.

For each present nav-chrome element, assert computed `position === 'fixed'` and numeric computed `z-index >= 100`. If class names differ, match by structural role (element that is a direct child of body, outside the .deck/.mag, functioning as progress/dots/counter/hints).

At 1920x1080, load the first slide in a fresh document before any pointer, focus, or keyboard input. The rail's exposed width must be <=46px and `data-rail-expanded` must not resolve to true. Fail any timer-driven peek or automatic expansion. The slide stage must begin at or to the right of the exposed spine, or otherwise prove a non-overlapping safe area.

At the delivery viewport: (a) the rail brand/open control, every chapter target, and previous/next buttons each measure at least 44x44px; (b) the first chapter target begins within 24px below the brand cell rather than being vertically centered; (c) clicking a visible non-navigation button, link, input, dialog control, `[data-interactive]`, or `[data-drill-target]` does not change the slide hash; and (d) while `[data-drill-open]` or a role=dialog surface is active, the rail is hidden, behind the modal, or has pointer-events:none.

Across combined stylesheet text and inline <script> text, at least one autofit safety-net marker must be present: `fitty`, `autoFit`/`autofit`, `resizeText`, or a `--min-font-size` custom property. Presence-only check; no ordering requirement.

Regex <style> text for a `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block that targets the slide/reveal selectors and forces `transition: none` (and opacity/transform to their resting values) with `!important`. Presence check on stylesheet text.

For every text-bearing element inside a slide/page, compute getComputedStyle(el).fontSize; flag any resolving below 16px, EXCLUDING documented label/caption/mono-badge roles: `.slide__label`, `.slide__subtitle`, `.slide__kpi-label`, `.pipeline__file`, `cite`, `caption`, table header cells, and any element whose class matches /label|caption|kicker|eyebrow|meta|badge|foot/. Measure at 1440x900 (widest authored clamp min).
For each `.slide--split` / `.slide--bleed`, assert computed padding-top/right/bottom/left are all `0px`. Inner panels keep their own padding — only the slide element itself must be zero.

For each `.page`, assert computed margin (all sides) and padding (all sides) are `0px`. Inner content elements (.page__half, .q, .cell) may pad; only the outermost `.page` boundary must be edge-to-edge.

Classify a page as dark if relative luminance of its computed background-color < 0.2 OR it carries `.page--dark`/`data-tint="dark"`. Assert: first `.page` and last `.page` in document order are both dark; total dark pages >= 3. Then render under prefers-color-scheme light AND dark and assert each dark page's computed background luminance is unchanged between schemes (dark is absolute, not mode-responsive).

Assert at least one `.page--stat` (or `.stat-xl` primary-number element) exists. For each, assert the primary number's computed font-size >= 100px (measured at 1440x900; authored `clamp(160px,22vw,360px)` satisfies this). Assert no two stat pages are adjacent in document order. Spacing cadence (every 4-6 pages) is NOT enforced.

Classify each `.page` by its layout-type modifier class. For each adjacent pair in document order, assert the layout-type classes differ (split->split is forbidden). Pages with no recognized layout class are excluded from the comparison rather than defaulted to a match.

For each adjacent pair of non-dark `.page` elements, compare `data-tint` attribute (preferred) or computed page-level background-color; flag any adjacent pair with an identical value. Dark panels are excluded from the comparison since they legitimately interrupt the rotation.
Count grid pages (`.page--grid`, or `.page` with >= 6 direct `.cell`/tile children). Flag if count > 1. The single-color-block bleed cap is NOT enforced here (no reliable signature — see dropped).

Static portion: a `.nav-dots` (or role-equivalent fixed dot strip) exists with exactly one `.nav-dot`/button child per `.page`; inline script registers a keydown handler covering ArrowRight/ArrowLeft/PageDown/PageUp/Space/Home/End that calls scrollBy/scrollTo with a `left` offset. Runtime portion: dispatch an ArrowRight keydown and assert `.mag.scrollLeft` increases by ~one viewport width; click a nav dot and assert scroll position changes to that page's offset.

After Mermaid render + autoFit: (1) the rendered `.mermaid svg` has no fixed `height` attribute and its getBoundingClientRect().width is within a few px of its `.mermaid-wrap` container width (fills, not tiny). (2) every `.nodeLabel` computed font-size >= 18px. (3) edge path stroke-width >= 2px. Soft signal in the same finding: rendered `.node` group count > 10 (slide budget is 8-10). Also verify the CSS override `.slide--diagram .mermaid svg{width:100%!important;height:auto!important}` (or equivalent) is present as a fallback.

Advisory predictor of overflow (authoritative gate is slide-viewport-fit-no-internal-scroll). Per slide type, flag when a documented max is exceeded: `.slide--content .slide__bullets > li` count > 6; `.slide--table .data-table tbody > tr` count > 8; `.slide--code .slide__code-block code` line count > 10 (trim leading/trailing blank lines); `.slide__kpis > .slide__kpi` count > 6; `.slide__kpi-val` textContent length > 6 chars; `.pipeline > .pipeline__step` count > 6; `.slide--quote blockquote` textContent length > 150 chars.

Validate the CSS PATTERN, not rendered px (per resolved contradiction: prose says '200px+' but authored CSS is clamp(100px,22vw,260px), which renders below 200px at narrow viewports). Assert the divider number's font-size is authored as a `clamp(min, vw, max)` whose max >= 160px (oversized) and that uses a viewport unit for the preferred term. Fail only a fixed small size or a clamp with a small max.

Classify each `.slide` by its type modifier (slide--title/content/split/diagram/dashboard/table/code/quote/bleed/divider) as a composition proxy. Flag any run of 3+ consecutive slides with the identical type class. This static run is a candidate only — pair with the composition-variety-visual llm pass for confirmation.

Static pre-check: inline script wires a fade (adds a faded/hidden class or sets opacity to 0) on both a ~4000ms timer and a keydown/click handler. Runtime: on fresh load dispatch a keydown and assert the hints element trends to opacity 0 (or gains its fade class) within one frame; separately, with no interaction, assert the same after 4000ms.

Deterministic pre-filter of the presentation-readability rule: for each slide/page, compute WCAG contrast between the resolved --text-dim color and the slide's resolved background; flag if ratio < 4.5:1. For nav-chrome elements, compute contrast against every distinct slide background (light and dark); flag if any falls below 3:1. Judgment about a single focal point is handled by the separate slide-single-focal-point llm pass.

Parse the default-export component's return(...). FAIL if the top-level returned JSX is a Fragment (`<>...</>` or `<React.Fragment>`). Also FAIL if the single root element's className lacks BOTH a `w-[<int>px]` and an `h-[<int>px]` Tailwind arbitrary-value token (or explicit inline width/height in px). The renderer measures exactly this one element and crops to its declared size.

Grep poster source for a live Mermaid dependency: an import of `mermaid`, a `<script src=...mermaid...>` CDN tag, or a `class="mermaid"`/`<pre class="mermaid">`-equivalent JSX node. Any match is a FAIL. The 1500ms rasterization wait is too short for Mermaid's async render, silently producing a blank diagram.

Grep poster source for Node fs APIs: `require('fs')`, `from 'fs'`/`from 'node:fs'`, `readFileSync`, `writeFileSync`, `fs.promises`. Any match is a FAIL — the poster is a headless-Chrome-rasterized bundle with no runtime fs; everything must be embedded at build time.

For each font family referenced by the poster: (a) if it is a Google Fonts family, require a `<link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/...">` (or preconnect+stylesheet) present as a JSX child INSIDE the returned root element (poster has no accessible document head; head-appended fonts won't apply); (b) if it references a Geist Pixel variant ('Geist Pixel Square/Grid/Circle/Triangle/Line'), require a `<style>` `@font-face` block inside the root with matching `font-family` and a `src: url('https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/geist@...woff2')` whose filename matches the variant. FAIL if a referenced family has no in-root source.

Render the poster in headless chromium at the declared canvas size. For every content element, read getBoundingClientRect relative to the root; FAIL if any right edge > width or bottom edge > height (element cut by the frame), or if any text node has computed text-overflow:ellipsis with scrollWidth>clientWidth (truncated). This is the deterministic half of the canvas-fit contract; pairs with poster-visual-fit-squint for rasterization-only clipping.

Grep the poster component for a live theme toggle: `matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme` driving render output, or `useState` bound to a theme-switch control, or a rendered light/dark toggle button. WARN if present — a poster is a static rasterized artifact; emit two separate posters instead of a runtime switcher.
WARN if a poster output filename does not match `.*\.poster\.(html|png|svg|pdf|jpg|jpeg|webp)$`. Keeps poster artifacts distinguishable from scrollable HTML output by name alone.

If the poster embeds known-slow async content AND the export invocation has no `--wait-for` value materially above the 1500ms default, WARN of an export race that can capture unhighlighted code / an unfinished chart frame. Prefer pre-rendered tokens/plain `<code>` with inline color spans for Prism inside posters.

For each `gsap.timeline(` call site with an object-literal options argument, require `paused: true`. FAIL if the options object omits `paused` or sets `paused: false`. Autoplay races the engine's seek-based capture and produces nondeterministic frames.

Parse the composition JS (acorn, not naive regex). Assert all of: (1) the `window.__timelines["<id>"] = ` assignment is NOT inside a setTimeout, async function, Promise executor/.then, or a DOMContentLoaded/load listener — it must run during synchronous top-level script execution; (2) each literal composition-id key is assigned exactly once (no duplicate registration); (3) the key string equals the root element's `data-composition-id` attribute (case-sensitive exact match). FAIL on any violation.

Grep all executable composition JS/CSS for forbidden patterns and FAIL on any live (non-commented) match: `Math.random(`; `Date.now(` / `new Date(`; `gsap.ticker.add(`; native WAAPI `<ident>.animate([` (array-literal first arg); manual `requestAnimationFrame(`; `repeat: -1` and CSS `animation-iteration-count: infinite`; engine-owned transport calls `tl.play()/.seek()`, `video.play()/audio.play()`, `.currentTime =`. Each breaks deterministic frame-seeked capture or hangs the render.

For each seed-PRNG factory call, extract the seed argument; FAIL if it is not a bare numeric literal (e.g. it contains Date.now(), Math.random(), a variable, or a function call). 'Allowed randomness' must stay deterministic across renders.

For every `<video>` in the composition, assert both a `muted` attribute (boolean or muted="muted"/"true") and a `playsinline` attribute are present. FAIL otherwise — audio must travel via separate `<audio>` for mixing, and unmuted/non-inline video breaks the engine's audio model.

If the file is a standalone root composition (no element in it carries `data-composition-src` and it is not referenced elsewhere as a sub-composition), assert the root is NOT a `<template>` and its content is not wrapped in a top-level `<template>`. If the file is loaded as a sub-composition (referenced via `data-composition-src="thisfile"`), assert its content IS wrapped in a `<template>`. FAIL on mismatch.

For each `<video>` whose src/<source> filename is not a silent pattern (not matching *-silent.*/*-noaudio.*/screen-recording heuristics), WARN if no sibling `<audio>` element anywhere in the document references the same base filename — audio should travel as `<audio>` for explicit mixing, not as a video's audio track.

Read data-duration/width/height on the composition root. Detect format (reel = portrait 1080x1920 or reel-labeled; long-form = landscape 1920x1080). FAIL (error) if a reel's data-duration > 60 (hard max). WARN if duration is merely outside the ideal band (reel 30–45s, long-form 60–180s) but within absolute limits, or resolution mismatches the format's target — such out-of-range renders are legitimized by an AskUserQuestion confirmation (see protocol).

If beat-labeled elements are present, read their data-start values and WARN only if present beats are out of the canonical sequence HOOK→PROBLEM→CONTEXT→MECHANISM→PROOF→RESOLUTION→CTA. Missing or merged beats are allowed (the 7-beat template is explicitly 'a template, not a rule').

Compute deltas between consecutive scene data-start values. WARN on any body-beat delta outside [1.2,1.8]s (excluding the HOOK/CTA first-and-last beats and the MECHANISM beat, which may dwell 3–5s). Also WARN if the delta distribution is bimodal (many sub-2s cuts AND several 5s+ dwell scenes) indicating an accidental reel/long-form pacing mix.

Identify full-frame cross-dissolve tweens and registered shader transition blocks with their time ranges. FAIL if any transition sits entirely within a single beat's span (not spanning a boundary), or if any beat boundary has more than one transition stacked. Dissolves/shaders are reserved for beat-to-beat transitions, never intra-beat.

Count words per .cap div. WARN if a 9:16 caption exceeds ~9 words (or a 16:9 caption exceeds ~16 words / 2 lines). Long captions must be split at a natural clause boundary in the script before TTS, never rewritten after the fact (which would break the verbatim rule).

In a headless render, read the caption's computed style: WARN if font-size outside 36–44px, font-weight != 600, background is transparent/light (not a solid dark fill), the bounding box spans ~100% of frame width (should not be full-bleed), or its box is not within the bottom third of the frame.

At each measured beat/keyframe, compute bounding boxes of visible text/primary-content elements. FAIL if any top edge is above frameTop+safeTop or any bottom edge below frameHeight−safeBottom, using aspect-appropriate margins: 9:16 = 100px top / 200px bottom; 16:9 = 60px top / 140px bottom. Protects against clipping by phone chrome and caption overlays.

Read computed margin/padding on the composition root/body/stage — assert 0 on all sides. FAIL if any wrapping container introduces a visible border/box-shadow/background distinct from the intended full-bleed canvas (gutters or a padded frame).
WARN if a primary-content element's bounding box extends below 0.667×frameHeight, or a caption's box extends above 0.667×frameHeight — the two reading zones must not mix.

Deterministic pre-filter: at each measured timestamp, count simultaneously-visible (opacity>0, on-screen) card-like content blocks (bordered/backgrounded containers with independent text) above a size/prominence threshold. WARN on any timestamp with 3+ such blocks visible — reel frames should present one focal element, not competing cards. (An LLM may confirm the flagged frame genuinely reads as competing focal points.)

In a headless render, read computed fontSize/fontWeight/letterSpacing/textTransform per role class and WARN when outside the documented table: hook-stat 180–260px/600–700; hook-claim 80–120px/500; beat-title 60–80px/500; body-copy 32–48px/400; caption 28–36px/600; kicker 18–22px/500 mono ALL-CAPS 0.12em. Enforces the loud, glance-legible hierarchy.

Count words in each reel body-copy block; WARN if it exceeds ~25 words (beyond ~1–2 lines at 32–48px on a 1080px canvas). Paragraph-length prose belongs in long-form, not a fast-cut silent-autoplay reel.

Assert `<span class="w">` word spans already exist in the final emitted HTML for any element targeted by a .w tween. FAIL if the composition builds these spans at runtime (e.g. textContent.split(' ').map(...) then innerHTML=/appendChild) — Hyperframes captures frame-by-frame and runtime-generated spans can be missing on early frames.

Extract GSAP tween start-times targeting node-N / arrow-N / label-N classes. WARN if the staged order is violated: all node-N reveals should precede all arrow-N reveals, which should precede all label-N/mask reveals, so the diagram builds up legibly.

Extract the target scale value in GSAP from/to tweens on still-image elements. WARN if the final scale exceeds 1.15 or the start scale is below 1.0 (delta larger than the documented 1.0→1.08–1.15 band) — large deltas 'look seasick.'

checks.evidence: The page embeds an inline UI demo media element.
checks.fix_hint: For inline demo media, assert a `

checks.evidence: The page has a demo `<video>` (identified by a data:video/webm;base64 source).
checks.fix_hint: For every inline demo `<video>`, assert the boolean attributes `autoplay`, `loop`, `muted`, and `playsinline` are all present so the clip behaves like a silent looping GIF-replacement in every modern browser. FAIL if any is missing.

checks.evidence: The page inlines a demo webm as a base64 data URI.
checks.fix_hint: Estimate the decoded byte size of the base64 demo video data URI. FAIL if > 2MB (inlined data URIs above this make the self-contained HTML sluggish). Additionally WARN if the source clip duration exceeds ~20s (long demos should link externally / use a share link). Fix by reducing frames, fps, scale, or demo length.

checks.evidence: Page contains a code-review or plan-review block, detected by the presence of at least TWO of the four category headings {Good, Bad, Ugly, Questions} (case-insensitive, whole-word) inside one review section. Skip entirely if fewer than two are present (page is not a review artifact).
checks.fix_hint: Within the detected review section, assert all four category sub-blocks exist with headings matching /^(good|bad|ugly|questions)\b/i. For each of the four, assert it is non-empty: it must contain at least one item/card child element OR the literal case-insensitive text 'None found'. Fail if any of the four category headings is absent, or a present category is empty and does not say 'None found'. This catches silent omission of a category (reads as 'not checked' rather than 'nothing found').

For each decision-log card, read its confidence level. Assert: high -> computed border-left-color resolves to the ok/green status token; medium -> border-left-color resolves to the blue token AND the card text contains 'inferred' (case-insensitive); low -> border-left-color resolves to the amber/warn token AND the card text contains the substring 'not recoverable' (case-insensitive, fuzzy). Fail on any mismatch between the stated confidence and its required color+text pairing.

checks.evidence: Output contains a fact-check verification summary, detected by a heading or class matching /verification summary/i. Skip if absent (presence is enforced separately as a protocol obligation, since the engine cannot reliably tell an arbitrary HTML file is a fact-check target).
checks.fix_hint: Within the verification-summary region assert all four data points are present: a total-claims-checked count, a confirmed count, a corrections list-or-count, and an unverifiable-claims mention. Assert every claim-status label used is drawn only from {Confirmed, Corrected, Unverifiable} (no other status words like 'Wrong'/'Partial'). If all three sub-counts and the total are numerically parseable, assert confirmed + corrected + unverifiable == total. Fail on a missing data point, an out-of-vocabulary label, or a count that does not reconcile.

checks.evidence: A <table> uses the sub-640px stacked-row degradation pattern, detected by either class 've-table' OR the page CSS containing an @media (max-width:640px) rule that sets a table td to display:block and uses content:attr(data-label) in a ::before. Do NOT run on tables that only scroll horizontally (wrapped in .scroll-x / overflow-x:auto) — those keep normal columns.
checks.fix_hint: For each in-scope table, assert every <td> inside <tbody> has a non-empty data-label attribute. A missing or empty data-label silently breaks the mobile stacked layout (the ::before label disappears and rows become unreadable).

Collect the computed primary font-family (first named family, ignoring generic keywords system-ui/sans-serif/serif/monospace) for every visible text node. FAIL when the count of distinct NAMED families exceeds 4. A dedicated monospace stack for code counts as one family, not a violation by itself.

checks.evidence: Page exposes at least two distinct type roles (a largest heading and body copy) that are not part of a dense data table.
checks.fix_hint: Read computed font-size for the largest heading and for body copy (and, where present, adjacent heading levels h1/h2/h3). Compute adjacent ratios. FLAG when an adjacent pair's size ratio is <1.25 AND font-weight is equal AND color is near-identical — i.e. no dimension of hierarchy (size, weight, or color) meaningfully separates the roles. This is the mechanical complement to the visual-hierarchy dimension of the artifact review.

Find short (≤~6 word) label-like elements with computed text-transform:uppercase (eyebrows, badges, nav labels, kickers) whose computed letter-spacing is `normal` or 0. FLAG — untracked all-caps reads as an unstyled default; capitals need ~0.05–0.12em tracking.

Parse clamp(min,preferred,max) on font-size for body/heading roles; normalize min/max to one unit. FLAG when max/min > ~2.5 (breaks zoom/reflow) OR when max exceeds ~6rem/96px on a hero/display heading (shouting, not designing).

The skill MANDATES Google Fonts <link>s — this check never bans the link, it only requires non-blocking load. FLAG @font-face blocks missing `font-display` entirely (defaults to auto/block → FOIT) and Google-Fonts <link>/@import URLs missing `&display=swap`.

FAIL when the viewport meta content contains `user-scalable=no` or `maximum-scale=1(.0)?` — an accessibility-breaking app-boilerplate default that never belongs on a static explainer/slide/magazine page.

For each text node, resolve the nearest non-transparent ancestor background. When that background's OKLCH chroma >~0.05 (a real accent color) and the text color is a mid-tone (L 0.4–0.7) near-zero-chroma gray — not a tint/shade of the background hue, not near-white/near-black at reduced alpha — FLAG as washed-out.

For each informational text node, resolve effective text color and the first opaque stacked-ancestor background; compute the WCAG relative-luminance contrast ratio. FAIL when font-size<24px (or <18.66px bold) with ratio<4.5:1, or ≥24px/≥18.66px-bold with ratio<3:1. Test both light and dark renders. Catches the pale-elegant-gray failure that is the single biggest reason AI designs read as hard to read.

checks.evidence: Document has focusable/interactive elements (a[href], button, input, [tabindex], summary).
checks.fix_hint: FAIL when `outline: none|0` is applied to a focusable selector (a/button/input/[tabindex]/summary) or a global reset (*, :focus) AND no overlapping `:focus-visible` (or `:focus`) rule supplies a visible replacement (a non-none outline, a contrasting box-shadow ring, or a border/background change).

FAIL when a class/selector defaults content to opacity:0 / visibility:hidden and a companion selector (same base + .in-view/.visible/.revealed/.active) restores it via JS `classList.add`, AND there is neither an `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` rule forcing the visible state nor a <noscript> override. PR #489: One document harness for the clinician note, UAP, FMM and Four Horsemen
Function-Health/function-intelligence, head 3758b0901c. A guided tour of the change, then how far to trust it: 25 Proven, 5 Backed, 5 Asserted, 3 Gap.
Orientation: what the PR does and why
This PR replaces four document pipelines with one harness, cr docgen --kind {note,uap,fmm,4h}.
Before this PR, each pipeline had its own CR loader, checks, repair and judge wiring.
The harness runs one loop for each kind. It projects a draft and reflects on it. An editor repairs the findings, and the loop keeps or reverts each round.
Type pins and a boundary script make the pipeline rules static, and anti-gaming rules stop the editor from hiding a problem without a repair.
The result is one set of contracts and fewer failures in the note, at a higher cost for each document.
